scope.interpretation: All ordered context pairs with at least one focus endpoint, including diagonals and background nodes.

BPL.definition: A finite probabilistic Turing machine with a read-only binary input and fresh independent fair coins, using O(log(n+2)) work cells on every prefix of every random computation and halting within one fixed polynomial on every input and coin sequence. Yes acceptance≥2/3; no acceptance≤1/3.
critical_exclusions: Two-way access to an uncounted random tape
Almost-sure halting without a worst-case polynomial clock
Separate time and space algorithms instead of simultaneous bounds

UL.definition: A finite binary nondeterministic machine uses O(log(n+2)) workspace and one polynomial all-branch clock. Every input has at most one accepting computation path; membership means exactly one. Count paths with transition-list multiplicity, not distinct reachable configurations.
critical_exclusions: US-style exact-one tests allowing multiple accepting paths on no inputs
StrongUL/StrongFewL restrictions on all configuration pairs
UL.complement: not asserted; coUL is not presently a context node

PL.definition: Polynomial-time logarithmic-space fair-coin computation with acceptance probability strictly greater than1/2 exactly on members (≤1/2 on nonmembers). Equivalently positive GapL, where GapL is a difference of two polynomial-clocked #L accepting-path counts.
critical_exclusions: Arbitrary branch-degree acceptance fractions without a fair-coin or GapL equivalence
Identification with every bit of determinant/#L
PL.complement: self; use integer gap shift to handle equality at1/2

ExistsR.definition: All total binary languages polynomial-time many-one reducible to finite binary encodings of existential real formulas with integer/rational coefficients, Boolean combinations of polynomial equality/inequality tests, and finitely many real variables. Fix an ordinary explicit syntax, reject malformed encodings. Equivalent implementation: finite binary systems of quadratic polynomial equations over the reals.
critical_exclusions: Arbitrary real constants in the machine
A succinct encoding that denotes exponentially many constraints
Unit-cost real inputs as the benchmark universe

UniformNC1.definition: Standard U_E-uniform polynomial-size logarithmic-depth bounded-fan-in Boolean circuits; equivalently ALOGTIME on a finite random-access-input alternating Turing machine with O(log(n+2)) time on every branch. The address tape, branching and query conventions must be explicit.
critical_exclusions: DLOGTIME recognition of only the direct-connection language U_D
Replacing random access by a one-way sequential input

facts.justification: §2.3 states L⊆BPL; deterministic logspace machines ignore coins.
Forget the logarithmic workspace bound while retaining worst-case polynomial time and the same all-input bounded-error gap.
The abstract explicitly simulates polynomial-time two-sided-error logspace in simultaneous polynomial time and O(log² n) deterministic workspace.
A bounded-error polynomial-time logspace machine already satisfies strict-majority unbounded error.
A deterministic accepting computation is the sole accepting path; deterministic rejection creates none.
The p.6 definition and containment explicitly give UL⊆NL.

For a polynomial-clocked logspace nondeterministic machine, its accepting-path count f is #L. The GapL function f−0 is positive exactly when an accepting path exists. Proposition3 identifies its positive languages with PL.
Corollary6.3 gives NC² for probabilistic logspace; §2 defines logspace-uniform circuits. This embeds in the benchmark’s logspace-uniform NC.
NP⊆∃R is stated in the abstract. Explicitly reduce Boolean circuit satisfiability to real quadratic constraints: z(z−1)=0 for each wire, z=xy for AND, z=1−x for NOT, and force output1.
Canny’s abstract states that the existential theory of the reals is decidable in polynomial space; polynomial-time binary many-one reductions preserve PSPACE.

Use standard U_E-uniform NC¹=ALOGTIME. A deterministic depth-first traversal of the logarithmic-depth alternating computation tree stores a path and recomputes configurations in O(log n) workspace; AppendixD of GHR records uniform NC¹⊆DLOG.
Forget standard U_E uniformity of the polynomial-size logarithmic-depth circuit family.
PARITY has a balanced binary XOR tree with standard U_E uniformity, after replacing XOR by constant-size AND/OR/NOT gadgets. The Furst–Saxe–Sipser lower bound excludes even nonuniform AC0.

nonuniform_circuits_advice.review: All five new classes are recursive and lie in PSPACE. Every nonuniform endpoint contains arbitrary unary languages via one advice bit/constant circuit per length; old AC0⊄PSPACE therefore propagates to all30 incoming pairs. Each new class contains uniform PARITY, so all five outgoing AC0 directions are false. Other outgoing small-circuit/advice questions need actual lower-bound theorems.

other_space_parallelism.review: Checked exact NC² uniformity, SC simultaneity, logspace randomness, ordinary versus strong unambiguity and BQL polynomial time. Neither BPL⊆LogCFL nor PL⊆LogCFL/SC nor UL⊆SC/BPL/BQL follows from the admitted chains. UniformNC1=L remains a distinct candidate.

counting.review: The four new small-resource endpoints lie in P, so their outward counting inclusions follow the old baseline; ExistsR does not inherit a CH/PSharpP upper bound from PosSLP or square-root-sum membership. PL is GapL, not GapP or PP, and the RST PL hierarchy does not identify arbitrary determinant bits with PL.

polynomial_time_randomness_proofs.review: Small-resource inclusions follow P and the old baseline. NP⊆ExistsR supplies only the transitive lower side of the real class; no general PH upper or lower inclusion was supplied. ETR-PCP real-alphabet proofs do not instantiate the binary MA/AM interfaces.

quantum.review: Use separately reviewed quantum primitives. Quantum witnesses have exponentially many amplitudes; an exponential-dimensional real feasibility encoding does not establish QMA⊆ExistsR. Real witnesses are not automatically quantum proofs. Ordinary UL is not covered by StrongFewL⊆BQL.

larger_resources.review: The four small-resource endpoints lie in NC and hence P. Time hierarchy and the old PSPACE⊄NC fact propagate the corresponding separations. ExistsR⊆PSPACE gives EXPSPACE⊄ExistsR, but does not separate NEXP or EXP from ExistsR when their PSPACE relationship is unknown. Polynomial reduction closure provides the two new real-class padding implications.

new_internal.review: Every ordered pair among the five audited nodes was enumerated. UL and BPL both embed in PL, all four small-resource nodes embed in ExistsR through P⊆NP, and UniformNC1 embeds in the other four through L. Reverse directions are retained unless supported by the signed closure.

limitations: This is AI-assisted literature review, not a human expert certificate and not a proof that every unresolved pair was historically open.
All585 incident pairs are enumerated and screened through the stated family arguments; searches and primary statements are selective, not585 independent literature searches.
The overlay assumes the cross-dossier quantum and counting seeds listed explicitly. It must be recomputed after the complete merged baseline and conditional rules are imported.
No automatic independence-from-ZFC literature conclusion is inferred from failure to find an ordinary containment.

Canonical Lean models still need an independent equivalence/encoding review. Literature facts are valid for the specified standard models, not arbitrary implementations with similarly named predicates.

UniformNC1 regular-padding closure was deliberately not imported. Its E/NE inclusion premises already contradict known facts through P; a direct U_E uniformity argument should accompany any future generic template.

Complexity Zoo live pages repeatedly failed; BPL and PL discovery mirrors were read, UL retrieval failed, and ExistsR discovery entry had no additional usable evidence. Primary papers, not mirror absence, determine the proposed labels.

No calibrated expected-error figure is supplied for this new extension. Largest remaining omission risks are the PL/LogCFL/SC interfaces, uniformity transfers, and ExistsR versus counting/proof systems; all need independent cross-review before release.
